title: Enhancing Depth Perception in SEM: Stereoscopic Imaging of Coccoliths by the Tilting Method
content:
Abstract
Stereoscopic visualization of extremely small objects remains a challenge in electron microscopy, where images are inherently two-dimensional. This article demonstrates practical approaches to three-dimensional (3D) perception at the nanoscale using coccoliths as exemplary specimens. Three species of the genus Discoaster were imaged by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and analyzed using the tilting method to generate stereoscopic datasets. Pairs of SEM images acquired at defined tilt angles were processed to produce stereo pairs, depth maps, and anaglyphic 3D images. These visualization techniques enhance the perception of fine surface relief, spatial relationships, and morphological complexity that are difficult to interpret from single SEM micrographs. The results highlight the value of stereoscopic SEM imaging for paleontological and nanostructural studies and illustrate how relatively simple acquisition and processing workflows can substantially improve 3D understanding of microscopic objects.
